# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first portrait browser game titled **Moonlit House: First-Year Broom Trial**. Preserve the source arcade traversal loop: a player uses a left virtual joystick to build speed across a large scrolling canvas, launches airborne when crossing rectangular gates at sufficient speed, taps one of three right-side action buttons while airborne, earns score only when landing cleanly after the action timer completes, is bumped airborne by hazards, and can end/restart through an overlay.

Reinterpret the game as a cozy gothic wizard-school adventure. The player is a first-year broom-riding student practicing spells in a moonlit castle courtyard. Gates are glowing charm arches. Action buttons are LUMOS, ACCIO, and SHIELD. Score is House Points. Hazards are cursed portraits and hexed trunks. The terminal overlay is class dismissal. Use procedural Canvas/CSS visuals: drifting stars, moving staircases, stone floor motifs, arched windows, spell particles, glowing charm arches, and a recognizable robed broom-rider silhouette.

Prioritize portrait mobile UX in the 4:7 to 9:16 range: readable HUD, thumb-reachable joystick and spell buttons, no tap-blocking decorative overlays, and clear restart/end state.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a single-page canvas arcade traversal game. The player steers an avatar with a left-side virtual joystick across a large 5000x5000 playfield. Moving fast enough through rectangular ramps/gates launches the avatar airborne. While airborne, one of three right-side trick buttons may be tapped; completing the landing after the trick timer expires awards score. Obstacles bump the avatar airborne and cause fumble feedback. A top-right end button opens a terminal overlay with the final score and restart button.

## Protected mechanics
- Left joystick pointer input, friction, acceleration, speed cap, and camera follow.
- Ramp/gate collision threshold: speed above 100 and rectangle overlap launches the player.
- Airborne physics: vertical velocity, gravity, z height, and landing checks.
- Trick semantics: buttons only work while airborne and only when no trick timer is active.
- Scoring: clean landing with combo adds `combo * 100`; failed landing during trick timer does not score.
- Obstacle contact: bump away, launch airborne, shake, particles, and hazard feedback.
- End/restart state flow and debug hooks for validation.

## Remix target
The source mechanics become a mobile-first wizard-school broom lesson in a moonlit castle courtyard. The player is a first-year wizard on a broom. Gates become charm arches. Tricks become spell practices: LUMOS, ACCIO, and SHIELD. Score becomes House Points. Obstacles become cursed portraits/hexed trunks. End state becomes returning to the dorm after class.

## Safe transformation surfaces
HUD copy, button labels, score labels, canvas entity drawing, palette, background layers, particle colors, audio assignment, typography, modal wording, and procedural scene motifs are safe to transform because they do not alter mechanics.

## Runtime approach
Plain HTML, CSS, Canvas, and vanilla JavaScript are used inline in `index.html` for stability and direct browser compatibility. Catalog-approved Google fonts and audio URLs are used as safe enrichment.
